risks.note: Over 91% of revenue is derived from a single commodity category, pulses, exposing the Company to concentration risk should this segment face adverse conditions.

Prices of tea, rice, wheat and pulses are inherently volatile, driven by monsoon performance, domestic and global supply-demand dynamics, and government intervention (MSP, buffer stock operations, import/export policy), which may adversely affect trading margins.
Frequent changes in Minimum Export Price, export duty, stock-holding limits and import tariffs on food grains and pulses can significantly impact the Company's ability to plan and execute trades.
Trade receivables represent a significant proportion of current assets, exposing the Company to delayed realisation or default by trade counterparties.
The trading business is working-capital intensive, funded through internal accruals and short-term borrowings; tightening credit availability or rising interest costs could impact profitability.
Pulses trading relies on imported material given India's large net import dependence, indirectly exposing the Company to global price and currency fluctuations.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Government focus on self-sufficiency in pulses (Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses) is expected to gradually improve domestic availability and moderate price volatility for the Company's largest revenue segment.
- Record wheat and paddy output with an active MSP procurement regime is expected to keep raw material availability comfortable for wheat and rice trading, though downstream prices may stay range-bound given elevated government stock levels.
- Sustained global demand for Indian tea, together with the Tea Board's export target of 300 million kg for calendar year 2026, is seen as an opportunity to scale up the Company's relatively small tea trading operations, subject to compliance with evolving international quality and residue-limit norms.
- Rising domestic consumption of food grains, tea and pulses driven by population growth, urbanisation and rising per-capita incomes.
- Expanding e-NAM and digital agri-marketplaces and improving rural logistics/warehousing infrastructure, which can reduce transaction costs and improve price discovery.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Over 91% of revenue is derived from a single commodity category, pulses, exposing the Company to concentration risk should this segment face adverse conditions.
- Prices of tea, rice, wheat and pulses are inherently volatile, driven by monsoon performance, domestic and global supply-demand dynamics, and government intervention (MSP, buffer stock operations, import/export policy), which may adversely affect trading margins.
- Frequent changes in Minimum Export Price, export duty, stock-holding limits and import tariffs on food grains and pulses can significantly impact the Company's ability to plan and execute trades.
- Trade receivables represent a significant proportion of current assets, exposing the Company to delayed realisation or default by trade counterparties.
- The trading business is working-capital intensive, funded through internal accruals and short-term borrowings; tightening credit availability or rising interest costs could impact profitability.
- Pulses trading relies on imported material given India's large net import dependence, indirectly exposing the Company to global price and currency fluctuations.
- Erratic monsoons, droughts or excess rainfall in key growing regions (such as the Assam rainfall deficit in January-February 2026) can affect crop output, quality and availability of key traded commodities.
- The agri-commodity trading business is highly fragmented and competitive, with numerous organised and unorganised players exerting continuous pressure on trading margins.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue prudent working capital management, diversification across commodities, and leveraging its network of subsidiaries and associates in the tea plantation and trading space to strengthen overall business resilience.
- Monitor monsoon trends, MSP and trade-policy announcements, and global commodity price movements, calibrating trading strategy, inventory positions and product mix accordingly.
- Deepen relationships with the Company's subsidiaries and associates to enable backward integration and better quality control.
